title: Stalled on-prem operator upgrade due to KV cache corruption — backup & customer restore playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: During a scheduled v3.6.1 operator upgrade at two customer sites (AcmeFin pilot and BetaRetail), the operator reconcile loop stalled after Helm applied new CRs. Investigation shows the operator's KV cache on the node was in a corrupted state (partial key overlap + tombstones) which caused reconcile handlers to spin and fail liveness probes, leaving tenants partially upgraded and blocking workloads. This ticket captures an immediate remediation playbook (backup, safe restore, operator restart order), short-term hotfix for v3.6.1, and longer-term detection/tests to prevent recurrence.
root_cause_summary: A race between Helm post-upgrade hooks that pruned CR fields and the operator's KV cache compaction produced inconsistent keys. When the operator resumed reconcile it attempted to reconcile using stale/partially-compact keys which tripped a code path that didn't handle tombstone markers, causing repeated reconciliation errors and eventual controller stall.
reproduce_steps: Provision a local on-prem cluster matching customer config (k8s 1.26, CRD v1beta annotations enabled)
Seed KV store with synthetic keys containing overlapping prefixes and tombstones (see scripts/kv-corrupt-sim.sh in repo)
Install operator v3.6.0, create test tenant resources, validate healthy reconciles
Run helm upgrade to v3.6.1 with the post-upgrade pruning hook enabled
Observe operator logs: repeated reconcile failures with stack trace referencing kv_cache.go:line and tombstone handling
Confirm controller restart or manual kv cache flush recovers tenant state
immediate_mitigation: Apply emergency runbook: take KV snapshot (kubectl exec nodeagent -- tar /var/lib/redwood/kv/snap -O > /tmp/kv-snap.tar)
Scale down operator deployment to 0 to stop reconcile loops (kubectl scale deployment/redwood-operator --replicas=0)
Run safe KV repair: run jobs/kv-repair.sh on affected node to normalize tombstone markers
Re-install operator with --unsafe-disable-prune-hooks=false (disable prune hooks) then scale operator back up
If operator fails to recover, restore KV from snapshot to a clean node and reattach tenant workloads following customer-approved window
Notify customers (AcmeFin/BetaRetail) with ETA and remediation steps, offer priority support call
hotfix_actions: Backport patch to operator reconcile: guard against tombstone keys by adding null-check and retry with compacted view (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/1892)
Add Helm pre-upgrade validation hook to detect overlapping prefixes in KV (chart change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/431)
Ship emergency release private-operator-3.6.1-hotfix1 that disables prune hooks by default for on-prem installs
Publish coordinated release notes and customer-facing mitigation guide
long_term_fix: Implement transactional KV snapshotting in nodeagent and expose explicit pre-upgrade snapshot API
Add CI e2e test that runs helm upgrade with seeded KV corruption scenarios to ensure operator recovers
Enhance observability: new metric operator.kv.tombstone_count and alert when tombstone spikes during upgrade windows
Design and ship a safe-rollforward operator mode that pauses destructive post-upgrade hooks until operator confirms KV integrity
Update private deployment onboarding docs to require automatic nightly KV compaction or operator-managed compaction windows
